operation.description: Return a combined agenda between `from` and `to` (at most 93 days, both included): due tasks and, from other modules, invoice and purchase invoice due dates, quote and pro forma expiries, recurring invoice runs, tax deadlines, absences and holidays. `sources` chooses the layers. Every layer also needs the read scope of its own resource and its module (for example `invoices:read` for invoice due dates, `absences:read` for absences); layers the key cannot read are left out without an error, and `sources` in the response lists the layers actually served. `assignee_id` (`me` or a member id) filters the task layer. The whole window is returned in one page.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First day of the window (`YYYY-MM-DD`, included). Required.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last day of the window (`YYYY-MM-DD`, included). Required. The window spans at most 93 days: a longer or inverted window returns 400 `parameter_invalid_range` on `to`.

parameters.name: sources
parameters.description: Comma-separated layers to include: `tasks`, `invoice_due`, `purchase_invoice_due`, `quote_expiry`, `proforma_expiry`, `recurring_invoice_run`, `fiscal_deadline`, `absence`, `holiday`. Omit it to include every layer; an empty value includes none. Each layer also requires the read scope of its resource (for example `invoices:read` for `invoice_due`) and its module: layers the key cannot read are left out without an error, and the `sources` of the response lists only the layers actually served. An unknown layer returns 400 `parameter_invalid_enum`.

parameters.name: assignee_id
parameters.description: Only filters the `tasks` layer: `me` for the member who owns the API key, or the UUID of a member of your company. Any other value returns 422 `invalid_param_value`.

type.description: Machine-readable category of the error. Versioned by `Factuarea-Version`: from `2026-09-01` onwards the payment gate codes `payment_method_required`, `seat_charge_failed`, `gestoria_plan_required`, `employee_seat_payment_method_required` and `employee_seat_charge_failed` are served as `payment_required_error`; requests pinned to an earlier version keep receiving `invalid_request_error` for those five. `error.code` and `error.subcode` never change — branch on `code` if you want version-independent behaviour.

code.description: Stable error code, e.g. missing_api_key, insufficient_scope, parameter_invalid, invalid_status_transition. Full reference of every code, grouped by area: https://docs.factuarea.com/guides/errors/all.

subcode.description: Sub-code detailing the subtype within `code`. Present only on some errors, and only where `code` alone is ambiguous: on 409 duplication conflicts it pins the duplicate key (`code=resource_already_exists`, `subcode=tax_id_already_exists`), and on 402 payment errors it pins which gate rejected the call (`code=seat_charge_failed`, `subcode=seat_charge_failed`; `code=addon_required`, `subcode=webhooks_addon_required`). Like `code`, it is stable and invariant across locales and API versions.

message.example: No se ha proporcionado una API key válida en el header Authorization.
examples: No se ha proporcionado una API key válida en el header Authorization.

param.description: Field that caused the error (for parameter_invalid and similar invalid_request_error codes). On multi-field validation errors it points to the FIRST failed field; the full set lives in `errors[]`.

line_index.description: Zero-based position of the document line that raised the error, the same `N` as in a validation path `lines.N.field`. Present only when a domain rule rejects ONE specific line of the document (a product, variant, presentation, configuration or option that does not exist or is deactivated, a missing price or VAT rate, an exemption cause or regime key outside its catalog, a disbursement line carrying what it may not, a line total that does not match, …) and absent on every other error. It is additive: `param` keeps naming the field exactly as before, so a client can ignore `line_index`. Use it to highlight the offending line without parsing `message`.

errors.description: Present on 422 validation errors: ALL failed fields, one item per field (not only the first). Each item carries `param`/`code`/`message` plus the optional hints `expected_format`/`allowed_values`. Additive and backward-compatible — `error.param`/`error.message` still mirror the first failed field.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code for this field, derived from the failed validation rule (e.g. parameter_missing, parameter_invalid_format, parameter_invalid_enum).

message.description: Human-readable description of the field error. Localized (es/en/ca) when its `code` belongs to the stable catalog.

expected_format.description: Expected format hint (e.g. `YYYY-MM-DD`, `uuid`, `email`, `url`). Only present when the failure is a format error.

allowed_values.description: Legal values of the enum. Only present when the failure is an enum/`in` error.

details.description: Structured details about the error, present only on some errors and with a shape that depends on the case. On 409 duplication conflicts (subcodes `tax_id_already_exists`, `external_id_already_exists`, `sku_already_exists`) it carries `existing_resource_id`, the UUID of the resource that already exists. On 402 `payment_required_error` responses caused by a missing payment method it carries `payment_setup_url`, the Billing Portal link that unblocks the operation. On the 422 subcodes raised inside the domain it carries the hint of that case: `allowed_values` (rejected value outside a closed catalog), `offending_field` (field a disbursement line may not carry) or `expected` + `received` (line total checksum mismatch).

operation_id.description: Operation in the authenticated company that must be resolved before another employee-seat mutation.

row_errors.description: Employee-batch validation failures identified by the stable row_id; no employee was charged or created.

field_errors.description: Review fields that must be corrected before a purchase scan can be converted. Keys use public identifiers, for example supplier_id or lines.0.tax_rate.

existing_resource_id.description: UUID of the pre-existing resource that triggered the conflict. Resolvable with a `GET /v1/{resource}/{id}` without an extra `find_by_*` call. Only present on 409 duplication conflicts.

payment_setup_url.description: Billing Portal URL where the payment method can be set up. Only present on 402 errors caused by a missing payment method (`payment_method_required`, `employee_seat_payment_method_required`); once the payment method is on file, retrying the same call succeeds. Absent on the other 402 codes (declined charge, plan or add-on required).

allowed_values.description: Legal values of the closed catalog the rejected value does not belong to. Present on the 422 subcodes that validate against a catalog inside the domain (`line_type_invalid`, `correction_code_illegal_for_original`). Note that a 422 raised by request validation reports the same hint per field in `error.errors[].allowed_values` instead.

offending_field.description: Name of the line field that made the operation illegal. Present on 422 `suplido_line_cannot_carry_taxes`: a disbursement line (`line_type: "SUPLIDO"`) may not carry VAT, withholding, surcharge, discount, regime key, exemption cause or product, and this names the one that was sent.

expected.description: Amount this API computed for the line. Present on 422 `line_total_checksum_mismatch`, together with `received`, so the rounding mismatch with your own ERP can be located without guessing.

received.description: Amount sent in `lines[].line_total`, which differs from `expected` by more than one cent. Present on 422 `line_total_checksum_mismatch`.

active_rules.description: Current active automation rule count on automation_active_rules_limit_exceeded.

limit.description: Plan limit reached, including the active automation rule cap on automation_active_rules_limit_exceeded.

resource.description: Resource whose quota was reached on plan_limit_exceeded, for example documents_year or users.

current.description: Current usage of the resource on plan_limit_exceeded.

period_end.description: End of the quota period on plan_limit_exceeded; null for resources without a period, including platform users.

doc_url.description: Link to error reference in docs.

PaginatedList.description: Cursor-paginated list envelope shared by every v1 listing endpoint. `data` holds the page items; `has_more` signals whether another page exists; `next_cursor` is the cursor to pass back for the following page. Treat it as strictly opaque: send it through verbatim, never parse it and never assume a format — it is not the same across listings, and each listing documents its own cursor parameter. Concrete listings narrow `data` to their resource type via `allOf`.

has_more.description: Whether more pages are available after this one.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or `null` when `has_more` is `false`. The example below shows the shape used by most listings; others return a different one, so pass the value back verbatim instead of validating it.

PaginatedList.title: PaginatedList

AgendaList.description: Every agenda item of the window in one page (`has_more` is always `false`), plus the layers served.

data.description: Items ordered by date, type and title.

has_more.description: Always `false`: the whole window is returned at once.

sources.description: Layers actually served: the requested ones that the API key can read (scope and module).

AgendaItem.description: An item of the combined agenda: a due task, a document due date or expiry, a recurring run, a tax deadline, an absence or a holiday.

id.description: UUID of the source entity, or a stable identifier for tax deadlines and holidays.

object.description: Stripe-like discriminator. Always `agenda_item` for this resource.

title.example: Integrar la pasarela de pago en el checkout
examples: Integrar la pasarela de pago en el checkout

status.description: Status of the source entity, or `null`.

url.description: Path of the item in the Factuarea app.

task.description: Task details, only in the `tasks` layer; `null` otherwise.

assignee_id.description: UUID of the assigned member, or `null`.

board_status.description: Board status: `planned` (backlog), `active` (in a column of the board) or `archived`.

fiscal.description: Tax deadline details, only in the `fiscal_deadline` layer; `null` otherwise.

task_id.description: UUID of the task generated for the deadline, or `null`.

FactuareaVersion.name: Factuarea-Version
FactuareaVersion.description: Pin the API version (`YYYY-MM-DD`, Stripe-style date versioning) for this request; omit to use the key's pinned version, or the latest if none. Unsupported version → `400 unsupported_api_version`; malformed → `400 parameter_invalid_format`. The effective version is echoed in the `Factuarea-Version` response header. See the [Versioning guide](/guides/versioning).

XActiveProfile.name: X-Active-Profile
XActiveProfile.description: Operate on behalf of a child company (gestoría master key): pass its public `id` (UUID v7) and the request runs against that child's data without changing the key's scope, tier or environment (omit to use the key's own company). Invalid UUID → `400 parameter_invalid_uuid`; unknown or non-owned id → `404 profile_not_found`. See the [Acting on behalf guide](/guides/acting-on-behalf).

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Client-generated opaque key (up to 255 characters; UUID v7 recommended) that makes retries safe: the first response is cached and replayed for repeats without re-executing the mutation. Reusing a key with a different body returns `409 idempotency_key_reused`. See the [Idempotency guide](/guides/idempotency).
